channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Georgia's ruling party moves to outlaw five major opposition parties
item.description: Georgia's ruling Georgian Dream party is initiating proceedings to ban five of the country's largest opposition parties. This move, which began hearings at the Constitutional Court on October 21, is seen as an authoritarian drift that could push a significant portion of the opposition out of the legal political sphere ahead of the 2028 parliamentary elections.

item.title: Industrial accident disrupts work at Tajikistan's Rogun Dam
item.description: An industrial incident occurred at Tajikistan's Rogun Dam on October 21, disrupting construction work. Conflicting reports suggest either no injuries or at least five workers were hurt. State officials claim no one was harmed, while RFE/RL reports, citing witnesses, indicate a more serious situation with workers trapped.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans home delivery of license plates and car documents by 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to launch home delivery of state license plates and technical passports for vehicles starting December 1, 2026. The country also anticipates a 27% increase in regional electricity demand by 2030, requiring immediate preparation of capacities and networks to support new factories and growing cities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Build Nearly 70 Medical and 50 Social Facilities in Regions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Parliament Committee on Regional and Infrastructure Development discussed implementing the President's directive on modernizing infrastructure. The committee supports the initiative to declare the upcoming year a year of nationwide construction. Plans include building approximately 70 medical and 50 social facilities across the regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts Smart Nursery Technologies in Cooperation with South Korea
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing smart nursery technologies in partnership with South Korea as part of the 'Yashil Makon' ('Green Space') national project. This initiative aims to increase green areas to 30% and enhance the efficiency of growing planting material. The project involves establishing 28 modern nurseries to combat desertification and climate change.

item.title: Fourth Central Asia Inter-Parliamentary Forum Opens in Dushanbe
item.description: The Fourth Inter-Parliamentary Forum of Central Asian countries has opened in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Delegations from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Kyrgyzstan are attending. The forum, themed "Unity for Peace, Security, and Prosperity of Central Asia," aims to foster regional cooperation.

item.title: CIS Agreement Ratified to Combat Evasion of Debt and Assets Abroad
item.description: Russia's Federation Council approved the ratification of a CIS agreement on data exchange for enforcing court decisions. This pact will simplify debt collection and make it harder for debtors to hide assets internationally by facilitating information sharing among member states.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Presidents Discuss Strengthening Bilateral Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara. They discussed strengthening Uzbek-Turkish strategic partnership in political, economic, and cultural spheres. Key points included establishing a high-level Business Support Council and expanding cooperation on promising projects. The leaders also exchanged views on international and regional agendas.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Belarus Expand Interregional Cooperation
item.description: Interregional cooperation between Uzbekistan and Belarus is expanding, with discussions held in Minsk focusing on the Tashkent region. Economic cooperation is a primary focus, building on the momentum from the Uzbek President's visit and the III Forum of Regions. Over 40 agreements were signed, yielding tangible economic results. Joint projects worth $55 million are underway, including wire production and poultry processing.

item.title: Industrial Growth in Uzbekistan's Akhangaran District Accelerates
item.description: Uzbekistan's Akhangaran district in the Tashkent region is prioritizing industrial development, deep processing of raw materials, and import substitution. Projects include producing high-voltage cables, copper pipes, and fittings. Enco Group's investment project totals $57.5 million, creating 350 jobs and enabling the first domestic production of 110-330 kV high-voltage cables.

item.title: Kazakhstan Woman Suspected of Forging Documents for Foreigners
item.description: In Ust-Kamenogorsk, Kazakhstan, a 28-year-old woman is suspected of forging three temporary residence permits for citizens of a neighboring country. The documents were not officially registered. Authorities are conducting a pre-trial investigation, and the woman is obligated to appear when summoned.

item.title: Turkish Media Highlights President Mirziyoyev's Role in Central Asian Integration
item.description: The Turkish publication Daily Sabah published an analytical article on the role of Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in strengthening good-neighborly relations and regional cooperation in Central Asia. The article emphasizes that thanks to Uzbekistan's balanced foreign policy, a new geopolitical environment has formed in the region, fostering mutual trust and a friendly atmosphere.

item.title: Staphylococcus and E. coli Found: Cause of Student Poisoning at Almaty Physics and Mathematics School Identified
item.description: An investigation at an Almaty physics and mathematics school revealed microbial contamination in some prepared foods, including E. coli bacteria in food samples and dish rinses. Disinfectant solutions also failed to meet standards. Four cafeteria workers tested positive for Staphylococcus aureus.

item.title: Astana to Experience Temporary Heating, Hot Water, and Electricity Outages on October 30
item.description: Parts of Astana will face temporary disruptions to heating, hot water, and electricity on Friday, October 30. These shutdowns are due to scheduled repairs on the heating network, electrical work, and tree trimming. Specific addresses affected have been published.

item.title: New Multidisciplinary Medical Complex with Oncology Center to be Built in Almaty
item.description: A new multidisciplinary medical complex, including an oncology center, is planned for construction in Almaty. The project aims to enhance healthcare infrastructure in the city.

item.title: Nearly 6,500 Drug Types See Price Reductions in Uzbekistan; Quality Concerns Raised
item.description: Uzbekistan has reduced prices for approximately 6,500 types of medicines, with some falling by 40-60%. The head of the Pharmaceutical Development Agency discussed price regulation, electronic prescriptions, and issues of over-prescription and corruption in the sector.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Turkish President to Strengthen Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a meeting with the Turkish President to discuss strengthening strategic partnership relations between the two countries. Key areas of focus included political-diplomatic, trade-economic, and cultural-humanitarian cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands IT Cooperation with Austria, Boosts Digital Exports
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively developing international cooperation in information technology and increasing digital service exports. A forum focused on technological partnerships, attracting foreign IT companies, and fostering business ties between Uzbekistan and Austria was held. IT Park Uzbekistan presented its export-oriented model and integration opportunities into the global market.

item.title: What Pollutes Our Air and How to Ensure a Healthy Future in Tashkent?
item.description: Tashkent's skies are visibly hazy, with dust, vehicle emissions, chaotic construction, and coal-fired greenhouses contributing to air pollution. While greenhouses are under scrutiny, focusing solely on them is insufficient. The Ministry of Ecology is investigating the primary sources of pollution to address the issue effectively.

item.title: Head of People's Council Outlines Key Tasks for Implementing President's Address
item.description: Yerlan Koshanov chaired an expanded meeting of the Presidium of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, focusing on implementing the President's address "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era." Koshanov emphasized the address's strategic importance and the need for active participation and accountability from council members to achieve national goals.

item.title: Construction Begins on 250-Bed Oncology Center with Robotic Surgery in Almaty
item.description: Construction has commenced on a new medical complex in Almaty, featuring a 250-bed oncology center and a diagnostic center. The facility, expected to be completed in 2028, will offer comprehensive cancer care, including diagnostics, surgery with robotic assistance, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy, according to the Ministry of Health.

item.title: Uzbekistan Refunded Over 16 Trillion Soums in VAT to Businesses in Nine Months
item.description: In the first nine months of the year, Uzbekistan refunded over 16 trillion soums in Value Added Tax (VAT) to businesses. Funds allocated to the manufacturing sector constituted 69% of the total amount. The service sector also received a significant portion of the refunds, according to the State Tax Committee.

item.title: Supreme Court Closes Case Against Former Defense Minister Ismail Isakov
item.description: The Supreme Court of Kyrgyzstan has closed the criminal case against former Defense Minister Ismail Isakov, related to the June 2010 events. The court found no criminal offense in Isakov's actions. The case, reopened in April 2021, concerned alleged facilitation of the illegal departure of Kadyrzhan Batyrov.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Meets Compatriots in Turkey
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Uzbek citizens living in Turkey. During the meeting, the head of state conversed with his compatriots, inquiring about their lives, studies, and future plans. The meeting aimed to connect with the diaspora and understand their aspirations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry Denies Disinformation Regarding Training Footage
item.description: The Ministry of Defense of Kazakhstan has commented on a video circulating online, which falsely claims to show a confrontation between foreign states. The ministry stated that the footage actually depicts training exercises of the Kazakh Armed Forces' special operations forces conducted from June to August 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Debates Death Penalty Reinstatement After Child Rape Case
item.description: Following a child rape case in the Namangan region, Uzbekistan is experiencing renewed debate over the death penalty. Some politicians advocate for its reinstatement, while others warn of increased risks to children. Human rights advocates oppose the move, citing the risk of judicial errors and the need for effective crime prevention beyond harsh punishments.

item.title: Japan's Water Project in Tajikistan Receives Lowest Rating Due to Poor Performance
item.description: A Japanese-funded water supply system in Tajikistan's Khatlon region, completed in 2013, provided residents with water for only 10.9 hours daily. An external evaluation commissioned by JICA rated the project 'D', the lowest possible score. Japan is now funding a new system in the Abdurahmoni Jomi district, applying lessons learned in metering and maintenance.

item.title: Almaty Mayor Orders Stricter Oversight of Infrastructure Project Implementation
item.description: Almaty Mayor Darhan Satybaldy has ordered enhanced control over the implementation of infrastructure projects in the city. The directive came during a meeting focused on the President's address, emphasizing increased citizen well-being through infrastructure development, digitalization, and entrepreneurship. Fourteen projects received 238 billion tenge in funding this year.

item.title: Wife Donates Kidney to Husband After He Suffered Cardiac Arrest in Shymkent
item.description: In Shymkent, a man named Nurzhan, who experienced clinical death after his heart stopped at work, received a kidney transplant from his wife. The surgery took place on October 21st. Doctors report positive changes in his lab results post-operation, and both spouses are in stable condition.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Arrives in Ankara for Working Visit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, accompanied by his wife, has arrived in Ankara for a working visit. He was welcomed at Etimesgut Airport by Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz and other officials. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral relations and discuss cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Recovers 617 Million Tenge for Cybercrime Victims
item.description: Over nine months, Kazakhstan blocked 5.5 billion tenge to combat cybercrime. Victims have voluntarily recovered 617 million tenge, according to the Ministry of Internal Affairs. The Ministry collaborates with the National Bank's Anti-Fraud Center to identify suspicious transactions and halt the movement of stolen funds. Over 76,000 incidents were initiated by law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Kazakhstan's maternity benefits to reach 4.3 million tenge by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's maternity benefits are projected to reach up to 4.3 million tenge by 2027, according to calculations based on a potential increase in the minimum wage. The highest payment for pregnancy and childbirth could approach 3.2 million tenge, or 4.4 million tenge for women in specific radiation zones. The actual amount received depends on the last 12 months' income for maternity payments and 24 months for childcare.

item.title: Ukraine Struggles to Destroy Russian Drone Base in Crimea, Satellite Images Reveal
item.description: New satellite images show Russia has converted a military airfield in Crimea into a drone launch base. Despite repeated Ukrainian attacks on Russian facilities in Crimea, the Gvardeyskoye airbase remains operational. An ex-Ukrainian soldier explains the difficulties Kyiv faces in neutralizing this strategic asset.

item.title: Rental Apartment Prices Decline in Kazakhstan, Almaty and Astana Remain High
item.description: Rental prices for apartments have decreased in several Kazakhstani cities, with a notable 50,000 tenge drop for two-room apartments in Pavlodar. However, rental costs in Almaty and Astana remain at a high level. While most cities saw price reductions in October, some, like Oskemen and Kostanay, experienced increases.

item.title: Almaty School Food Block Suspended Amidst Student Poisoning Investigation
item.description: The food block of the Republican Physics and Mathematics School in Almaty has been suspended for 60 days following a mass poisoning incident. While violations were found, the investigation into the exact causes is ongoing. Law enforcement is also involved.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enhances Control Over KazMunayGas Foreign Assets
item.description: Kazakhstan has included six foreign subsidiaries of KazMunayGas (KMG) in a list of strategically important economic sectors subject to state property monitoring. Among these is KMG International, which manages oil refineries in Europe. The decree, signed by Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov, takes effect on October 30.

item.title: Uzbekistan Investigates Reports of Mass Citizen Data Leak
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has launched an investigation into reports of a potential leak of citizens' personal data circulating on social media and Telegram. The probe, involving the State Security Service's Cybersecurity Center and AUTODOC company, aims to verify the authenticity and origin of the data.

item.title: Former National Security Committee Officer's 12-Year Sentence Overturned
item.description: A court has overturned the 12-year prison sentence of Manat Sarbasov, former deputy head of the Shymkent Department of the National Security Committee. He was accused of accepting a 70 million tenge bribe to provide patronage for a private school. The cassation court cited procedural violations in the original trial.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Arrives in Turkey for Working Visit
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov arrived in Ankara, Turkey, on October 29 for a working visit. He was met at the Etimesgut International Airport by Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz and other officials. Japarov is scheduled to attend the 13th Summit of Heads of State of the Organization of Turkic States.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prioritizes Long-Term Infrastructure Development Over Short-Term Gains
item.description: Kazakhstan's President has outlined a long-term vision focusing on infrastructure development, allocating approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by 2029 for schools, hospitals, cultural and sports facilities, and road and utility network upgrades. This strategic investment prioritizes sustainable development and future societal benefits over immediate populist measures.
